claims.text: The untreated eutectic HEA has a hierarchical microstructure consisting of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittle behavior.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries cause local stress concentrations and contribute to brittle fracture in the untreated alloy.
High-pressure torsion will refine the lamellar colonies.
High-pressure torsion will reduce inter-lamellar spacing.
High-pressure torsion will make the lamellar colonies more uniformly distributed.
High-pressure torsion will improve interphase-boundary coherency.
Refinement and improved boundary coherency will facilitate more uniform dislocation motion across the constituent phases.
Decreasing the distance between phase boundaries will enable dislocations to cross interfaces more readily rather than accumulate at them.
Reduced dislocation accumulation at interfaces will reduce local stress concentrations and microcracking.
High-pressure torsion will generate a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations.
The geometrically necessary dislocations generated by HPT will contribute to strain hardening and help maintain or increase strength.
HPT processing will markedly increase room-temperature tensile elongation relative to the untreated alloy.
HPT processing will maintain or increase yield strength and ultimate tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
Grain refinement strengthening and enhanced dislocation transmission are responsible for the predicted retention or increase of strength.
The predicted benefits apply at room temperature and tensile strain rates of approximately 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
Undesirable phase transformations, overheating, or excessive deformation could deteriorate the phase balance and negate the benefits of HPT.
